chapter: Learning from players; Jonah Jones lessons
title: The humility of teaching; why he doesn't advertise
summary: Hinton praises the humility; Maxwell recalls Buck and Jonah on the trumpet and teaching haggling parents.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, you were brave enough to want
that and that's the humility of becoming -- a very fine teacher.

I'm not that brave. I generally regret it and say, oh, God, I wish I hadn't told that. Because it's going to be anxiety. I get very anxious, this man's life in my hands. Buck and Jonah were sitting down in my studio one day and we were talking about playing trumpet. Jonah said, well, you know, if that's all a man's really got, your children grow up and leave home, your wife gets fed up with you. He said, the one continuity in your life is the trumpet, and if you can't do that, what have you got? And Buck said, yeah, that's it, you know. You spend more time on your music in your lifetime than you do on any other things.
Yeah. And I know just how they feel. I have nightmares about losing my teeth or something.
That's beautiful. That's a good story (inaudible).

I feel good about it, I really do. I don't tell it around too much. Now, Jonah I talk about because he told the newspapers and I have the clipping in my studio. But I don't tell around about Buck or that Harry Edison mentioned it, because they may not want that kind of thing going around. This on the tape is different.
You don't need that kind of publicity.
And they sort of notice you don't. And the sincerity -- they come to you, you're not advertising.

No, I don't advertise at all. Except sometimes people will hassle me on the phone or something, some woman will call up and want lessons for her kid, and I tell her, you know, what my price is. And she says, well, that's awful expensive for a beginner. And I said, I think so, too, why don't you go to so and so. And she'll start haggling, "Well, what right have you got --" I say listen, lady, I didn't ask you, you're asking me. I didn't come to you. And I'm lucky I'm in a position to have enough pupils I can say that, I don't have to put up with any of that stuff.
